newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis, Palestinians clash near Bethlehem.
newsitem.headline: Israelis, Palestinians clash near Bethlehem.

text.p: Israeli troops fired teargas on Thursday at hundreds of stone-throwing Palestinians protesting against Israel's building of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, witnesses said.
They said the Palestinians, taking part in a march, broke through Palestinian police barriers near the tomb of the biblical matriarch Rachel in Bethlehem which is guarded by Israeli troops.
There were no immediate reports of injuries. But witnesses said some 50 Palestinian stone-throwers were pelting Israeli soldiers with stones an hour after the unrest began.
Israeli soldiers fired teargas from behind barricades they had erected on the main street linking Bethlehem to Jerusalem.
They said about 40 Palestinian policemen struggled to stop the stone-throwing.
Israel enraged Palestinians when it broke ground on Tuesday for construction of 6,500 houses for Jews on a pine-covered hill on the southern outskirts of East Jerusalem. Protests had been peaceful.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat asked Palestinians to refrain from violence during protests against the settlement.

Clashes last September over Israel's opening of an archaeological tunnel near Islam's holiest shrine in Jerusalem began with stone-throwing but evolved into gun battles between Israeli soldiers and PLO security forces.
Sixty-one Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers were killed in the confrontations last September.
